No animation studio has undergone a more dramatic ideological shift in the last decade than Pixar. The company that gave us Toy Story, Finding Nemo, and The Incredibles, films built on duty, sacrifice, and traditional family love, gradually drifted toward progressive messaging starting around 2019. The result is a filmography with enormous variance: some Pixar films score as strongly traditional, others score as outright woke, and several fall in contested territory.

VirtueVigil has reviewed 7 Pixar films using the full VVWS weighted scoring system. Here they are ranked from highest woke score to lowest. This is not a ranking of quality. It is a ranking of ideological content, so you know what you are getting before you sit down with your family. We will continue reviewing the Pixar catalog as we expand our database.

#1 (Highest Woke Score) — Elio (2025)

VirtueVigil Woke Score: 18.0 • Trad Score: 24.0 • Verdict: TRADITIONAL LEAN • Score Margin: +6 TRAD

Elio carries the highest raw woke score of any Pixar film we have reviewed, yet its traditional elements outweigh them significantly, which is why it scores TRADITIONAL LEAN despite that heavy progressive scaffolding. The film had a turbulent production that included the removal of a non-binary character named Grazie Giorgio and significant reshoots, suggesting internal pushback against progressive elements before release. What survived is a largely warm sci-fi adventure about duty, belonging, and the courage to represent your people well. The woke score reflects the ideological freight in the setting and secondary character design. The traditional score reflects what the story actually says when it matters most.

#2 — Turning Red (2022)

VirtueVigil Woke Score: 17.85 • Trad Score: 4.55 • Verdict: WOKE • Score Margin: -13 WOKE

Turning Red is Pixar's most ideologically loaded film by margin, and it is not particularly close. The film's central thesis is that a 13-year-old girl should embrace her chaotic emotional self rather than honor her mother's traditional expectations, and the story frames parental authority as the villain and adolescent self-liberation as the goal. Director Domee Shi confirmed in interviews that the red panda transformation is an explicit puberty and bodily autonomy metaphor. The traditional score of 4.55 is the lowest of any Pixar film we have reviewed. Parents expecting a fun animated animal adventure are getting a film about rejecting parental guidance, and the film makes no attempt to hide that intention.

#3 — Toy Story 4 (2019)

VirtueVigil Woke Score: 17.2 • Trad Score: 8.0 • Verdict: WOKE LEAN • Score Margin: -9 WOKE

Toy Story 4 is technically brilliant and morally catastrophic. The first three Toy Story films built a complete moral universe around duty, purpose, and belonging to a child. Toy Story 4 asks a different question: what if purpose is actually about self-actualization? Woody abandons Bonnie, the child depending on him, to pursue his own fulfillment with Bo Peep. The lesson for children watching is the inverse of what the trilogy spent 20 years teaching. Your own happiness matters more than the people who depend on you. The woke score of 17.2 captures a film that dismantles the moral architecture it inherited and replaces it with a self-actualization framework that the original Woody would have rejected.

Read the full VirtueVigil review of Toy Story 4

#4 — Hoppers (2026)

VirtueVigil Woke Score: 16.0 • Trad Score: 18.0 • Verdict: MIXED • Score Margin: +2 TRAD

Hoppers is ideologically fascinating: a film that looks built for progressive audiences but repeatedly punishes its activist heroine for her methods. The environmental premise and Republican-coded villain are pure woke scaffolding. But Mabel's unchecked activism leads to violence, accidental killing, and near-catastrophe, and the film ultimately argues that dialogue and compromise work better than protest and confrontation. King George, the patient and forgiving elder figure, embodies traditional virtues and is consistently proven right. The result is a MIXED verdict with the traditional score barely edging out the woke score. Conservative families can enjoy Hoppers with some caveats, but they should be aware of the ideological framing in the first act.

#5 — Elemental (2023)

VirtueVigil Woke Score: 12.2 • Trad Score: 19.74 • Verdict: TRADITIONAL LEAN • Score Margin: +8 TRAD

Elemental is the sleeper traditional film of Pixar's recent catalog. Critics gave it a middling 74% and the discourse centered on its immigration allegory. But audiences gave it a 95%, responding to what the film is actually about: first-generation family sacrifice, the weight of parental expectations, and love earned through loyalty. Ember's entire story arc is built on traditional immigrant values: honor your parents, work hard, and build something lasting. The woke scaffolding is real, present in the environmental messaging and some representation choices, but the film's emotional core consistently pulls toward traditional values. The margin of +8 TRAD reflects a film that earns its family credentials.

#6 — Lightyear (2022)

VirtueVigil Woke Score: 10.22 • Trad Score: 6.65 • Verdict: WOKE LEAN • Score Margin: -4 WOKE

Lightyear is the Pixar film that generated the most cultural controversy relative to its actual ideological weight. The restored same-sex kiss between Alisha Hawthorne and her wife became the defining news item around a movie that mostly fails because it is a boring action film. The woke score of 10.22 reflects real progressive elements: the same-sex relationship, identity-first messaging, and Buzz's self-discovery arc framed as personal liberation from external duty. The negative score margin of -4 WOKE puts it in the same ideological territory as Toy Story 4, though with less emotional damage. Lightyear was banned in 14 countries over the same-sex kiss and earned Pixar's worst box office performance since the pandemic at the time of its release.

#7 (Lowest Woke Score) — Inside Out 2 (2024)

VirtueVigil Woke Score: 10.08 • Trad Score: 20.16 • Verdict: TRADITIONAL • Score Margin: +10 TRAD

Inside Out 2 is the best Pixar film in years and the clearest evidence that the studio can correct course when it wants to. After Lightyear, Strange World, and the box office stumbles of Elemental, Pixar went back to basics: make a story about feelings, make it emotionally honest, and trust the audience. The result was $1.699 billion worldwide, making it the highest-grossing animated film of all time at the time of its release. The traditional score of 20.16 reflects a film built on emotional honesty, the value of accepting difficult feelings rather than suppressing them, and a genuine understanding that growing up means learning to hold complexity without losing your core identity. The lowest woke score on this list and the highest traditional score by margin.

What the Data Tells Us About Pixar

The picture that emerges from these 7 films is complicated. Pixar is not uniformly woke. It is a studio in ideological flux, capable of producing Turning Red and Inside Out 2 within the same period, films that represent opposite ends of the values spectrum.

The pattern that emerges from the scores is instructive. When Pixar leads with story, it produces films that score well on traditional values. Inside Out 2 told a story about anxiety and identity and earned $1.699 billion. Elemental told a story about immigrant family sacrifice and found an audience that critics missed. When Pixar leads with message, the results look like Turning Red (a film that begins with ideology and works backward to story) or Lightyear (a film so focused on progressive representation choices that it forgot to be entertaining). The market has been sending this signal clearly and consistently. Elio's $21 million domestic opening, the worst in Pixar history, came after years of controversy about the studio's direction. Inside Out 2's $1.699 billion came when it set the discourse aside and made a film about what it actually feels like to grow up.
